text:
emma: quick heads-up — running into a scoping/impersonation oddity with the Node SDK when calling the streaming API across projects.

raj: what does "oddity" look like? token rejected? wrong project/model?

emma: token accepted by Redwood edge but requests get routed to the wrong project workspace (we see metrics/usage land in project-b not project-a). using service account impersonation via `generateAccessToken` on the control plane.

maria: are you passing `target_audience` / `aud` for OIDC or the `scope` list for OAuth? those behave differently for cross-project impersonation.

emma: here's the snippet:

```js
const token = await iamClient.generateAccessToken({
  name: 'projects/-/serviceAccounts/sa@project-a.iam.gserviceaccount.com',
  scope: ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform'],
  delegates: ['projects/project-b/serviceAccounts/impersonator@project-b.iam.gserviceaccount.com']
});
// then set Authorization: Bearer ${token.accessToken} on streaming socket
```

liam: hmm delegates spanning projects can cause audit/usage attribution to flip if the final principal is from a different project. The control plane attributes to the identity that ends up in the `sub`/`iss` claims.

raj: Node SDK detail — when we open a streaming connection we currently take the bare `accessToken` and attach it; we don't send any `x-org` override header. If the impersonation chain creates an `iss` from project-b, the runtime will attribute.

emma: so is the fix to impersonate into a SA that lives in project-a instead of delegating to project-b?

maria: two options: (1) keep the final impersonated principal in project-a (preferred), or (2) use a service-side exchange where control plane mints a token scoped/aud for project-a and returns it (requires backend change).

raj: also watch out for `aud` vs `scope` when mixing OIDC tokens vs OAuth access tokens. OIDC `id_token`/`aud` is checked by some middleware for project-targeting.

liam: side note for streaming reauth: we've seen Node clients not renewing the socket-level token properly because `onBearerExpired` only triggers on 401 frames, not on token TTL. Could lead to a stale principal staying attached.

emma: that might explain intermittent flips — socket kept running with the wrong impersonated principal after a rotation.

raj: quick repro suggestion: try minting a token with `aud` set to `https://api.redwood.example/v1` and no delegates, and see attribution. then repeat with delegates to project-b and compare.

emma: doing that now, will paste logs.

ci-bot: deploy-check — new SDK PRs that touch auth should include an e2e that validates usage attribution across org/project boundaries. :white_check_mark:

maria: fwiw, Python SDK wraps impersonation differently (it sets `target_audience` when requesting id_tokens for OIDC flows), so we should document the language differences in the auth guide.

emma: filing a quick doc issue: https://go/repo/issues/2345 — adds a section on cross-project impersonation gotchas + streaming reauth recommendations.

liam: pinging @raj for a small SDK change: can we add an explicit hook to set `x-redwood-project` on streaming open if present in the client config? would make attribution explicit.

raj: sure — I'll sketch a patch. If we add the header we need to validate it server-side (ignore if mismatched) to avoid spoofing.

emma: thanks. also, note about token TTLs: GCP impersonation tokens default 3600s. streaming clients should rotate proactively at ~80% TTL.

raj: agreed. i'll add a short TTL/refresh example to the Node README and a test in the e2e matrix.

emma: thanks all — will follow up in the doc issue with the logs. short-term workaround: avoid cross-project delegates for production streams.

liam: +1

maria: noted, adding a checklist item to our onboarding doc for service account placement and delegation rules.
